div.head: II Cn 79
div.ab: And se ðe land gewerod hæbbe on scire gewitnesse (⁊ se nolde oððe ne mihte, þe hit ær ahte), hæbbe unbesacen on dæge ⁊ æfter dæge to syllenne ⁊ to gyfenne þam þe him leofost si.
And se ðe land gewerod habbe be scyre gewitnesse, habbe he unbesacen on dæge ⁊ æfter dage to syllene þam þe him leofast sy.
Et qui terram adquietatam habet scyrę (id est comitatus) testimonio, habeat sine querela in die et post diem ad dandam ei quem plus amabit.
And se ðe land gewerod hæbbe on scypfyrde ⁊ on landfyrde be scire gewitnysse, habbe he unbesaken on dæge ⁊ æfter dæge to syllanne ⁊ to gyfane ðam ðe him leofast sy.
And se ðe land gewerod hæbbe on scire gewitnesse and se nolde oððe ne mihte, þe hit ær ahte, hæbbe unbesacen on dæge and æfter dæge to syllenne and to gyfenne þam þe him leofost si.

And he who, with the cognisance of the shire, has performed the services demanded from a landowner on expeditions either by sea or by land shall hold [his land] unmolested by litigation during his life, and at his death shall have the right of disposing of it or giving it to whomsoever he prefers.

And the person who, with the knowledge of the shire, has overseen an estate, and the previous owner would not or could not, shall hold it uncontested during his lifetime and afterward be entitled to give or grant it to whomever he prefers.
And he who has performed the obligations on an estate with the witness of the shire is to have it uncontested for his lifetime and to give it to whom he pleases after his lifetime.

Und wer unter Zeugniss der Grafschaft ein Landgut [in dessen Leistungen an den Staat] vertreten hat (indem der frühere Besitzer es nicht [vertreten] wollte oder konnte G), dürfe es unbestritten bei Lebzeiten und von Todes wegen veräussern und verschenken dem der ihm meist beliebe.

And whoever, with the witness of the shire, has defended an estate [in its obligations to the state] (since the former holder would not or could not [defend it], G), let him be allowed undisputed to sell and to give it away, in his lifetime and at his death, to whomever he most pleases.

note.label: cf. (similar issue)
note.quote: Wulfstan confronted something like this issue elsewhere: V Atr 32:3 ('D')

div.note: The bracketed words about the former holder are only in G; Liebermann thinks them not original.
The Nero text adds: “and he who owned it before would not or could not”.
hæbbe on: B adds scypfyrde and on landfyrde be

In London, British Library, Harley MS 55, and Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 383, this clause reads, “And the person who, with the knowledge of the shire, has acted in defense of the land, either in the navy or army, shall hold his property uncontested during his lifetime and afterwards be entitled to give or grant it to whomever he prefers” (And se ðe land gewerod hæbbe on scypfyrde and on landfyrde, habbe he unbesaken on dæge and æfter dæge to syllanne and to gyfane ðam ðe him leofost sy).
